name: Brocade-Throne

civilization.name: The Brocade Architects
civilization.notes: A species that encoded all knowledge into ornate physical structures. Their cities are essentially libraries, with every surface inscribed with data in patterns resembling brocade embroidery. Extinction cause unknown—cities show no signs of war or disaster.

geological_features: Ancient mountain ranges worn to rolling hills
specific_features: Alien ruins covering 12% of land surface with brocade-patterned inscriptions
Intact atmospheric processing systems still maintaining breathable air
description: Brocade-Throne is a generous terrestrial world with a climate and atmosphere almost indistinguishable from Earth's most temperate regions. Rolling green hills give way to deep fjords along the northern coastlines, and wide river valleys support lush vegetation that has reclaimed much of the planet's surface since its inhabitants vanished. The planet would be unremarkable among habitable worlds if not for what the Brocade Architects left behind: cities that cover twelve percent of the land surface, every wall and floor and ceiling inscribed with patterns of breathtaking intricacy.

The inscriptions cover every surface of every structure in continuous, unbroken patterns that xenoarchaeologists have determined are a form of data encoding. The Architects wrote their entire civilization onto their buildings—history, science, art, personal correspondence, everything woven together in patterns that resemble brocade fabric in their layered complexity. Reading these inscriptions has become the work of generations, with translation efforts revealing a species that valued beauty and knowledge above all else and saw no distinction between the two.

The mystery of their extinction is the planet's deepest puzzle. The cities show no signs of war, disease, plague, or natural disaster. Food stores were neatly organized, atmospheric processors were set to automatic maintenance, and the inscriptions simply stop mid-pattern, as though every Architect put down their tools at the same moment and ceased to exist. No bodies have been found. No final messages have been identified. The atmospheric processors continue to function after thousands of years, maintaining breathable air for inhabitants who will never return.

Brocade-Throne is now the largest archaeological site in human-explored space, with over forty research teams operating across the inscribed cities. The translation work has already yielded advances in mathematics and materials science, drawn from the Architects' encoded knowledge. But the central question persists: where did they go? Some researchers believe the inscriptions contain the answer, hidden somewhere in the billions of square meters of encoded text. Others suggest the Architects transcended physical existence, encoding themselves into their buildings along with everything else. The cities wait, patient and beautiful, their walls still speaking to anyone willing to learn the language of the dead.
